title: A/B, shadow, canary and feedback signals
summary: Online experiments test a new version on live traffic. Shadow traffic hides it from users, a canary exposes a small share, an A/B test randomises users to measure outcomes, and feedback signals feed triage. Pick by harm if the new version is worse, traffic volume and what quality signal exists without references.
useIf: Offline results look good but only real traffic can show user outcomes, drift or rare failures.
avoidIf: Harm from the worse version is high and you have no safe exposure path, or traffic is too low to detect the effect you care about.

explain.md: Online methods trade safety for realism. **Shadow** copies live requests to the new version and discards its answers, so users see nothing, but you get no user reaction. **Canary** sends a small share of users to the new version. An **A/B test** randomises users between versions and compares outcome metrics. **Continuous evaluation** scores sampled traffic with judges. **Feedback** (thumbs, edits, retries, escalations) is cheap, biased toward vocal users and best used to find new test cases. LangSmith automation rules, for example, can add low-feedback traces to a dataset [[r29]].

steps.title: Offline gate
steps.md: Golden set, safety and regression suites pass.

steps.title: Shadow
steps.md: Mirror a share of traffic. Score outputs. Users see nothing.

steps.title: Canary
steps.md: A small share of users. Stop-loss on safety, escalation, latency and cost.

steps.title: A/B
steps.md: Randomised split to measure outcomes with enough samples.

steps.title: Roll out or roll back
steps.md: Decide on the pre-agreed guardrails, not the best-looking chart.

explain.md: Azure Machine Learning traffic mirroring copies a share of live requests to a new deployment without changing client responses. The mirrored share is capped at 50%, an endpoint can hold one shadow deployment, it is not supported on Kubernetes online endpoints, and the default endpoint bandwidth quota is 5 MBps [[r36]]. No Foundry-native shadow feature turned up in a Microsoft Learn search on 2026-10-13, so for LLM apps expect to mirror at the gateway or in your own router. Foundry continuous evaluation (preview) uses Random or Intelligent sampling, defaults to 100 runs per hour and needs the Foundry User role on the project's managed identity [[r7]]. Intelligent sampling dedupes, filters broken traces and picks diverse ones without extra model calls [[r40]]. Online scoring runs asynchronously and uses judges because live traffic has no ground truth [[r30]].

explain.title: Samples per arm for an A/B test (two proportions, unpaired)

vars.v: z for alpha 0.05 two-sided and for power 0.80

explain.example: Near p = 0.80: d = 10 points needs about 251 per arm, d = 5 points about 1,004, d = 3 points about 2,788 (computed estimate with the same variance in both arms; 80% against 70% with each arm's own variance needs about 290; paired designs need fewer).

whereToUse: Swapping a model version where harm is possible
Changing prompts, retrieval or tools that alter user outcomes
Drift monitoring through sampled online scoring
Turning thumbs-down and retries into new offline cases
Cost and latency comparisons under real load

use: Offline gates pass and you need real-world evidence
You can define stop-loss metrics and rollback
Traffic is large enough for the effect you care about
avoid: Shadowing agents with write tools without mocking the side effects
Stopping an A/B test early because the chart looks good
Using thumbs-up rate as the only success metric
flips: Harm if worse is high: shadow first, then a tiny canary
Traffic is low: skip A/B, use canary plus sampled human review
Content cannot be read: score metadata and safety signals only

pitfalls.symptom: The shadow agent sends duplicate emails or writes duplicate records
pitfalls.cause: Mirrored requests executed real write tools
pitfalls.fix: Run the shadow with read-only or mocked tools, and compare tool calls instead of executing them

pitfalls.symptom: Thumbs-down jumped after a release, but offline metrics are flat
pitfalls.cause: A UI or latency change moved feedback, not the model
pitfalls.fix: Segment by version, check latency and compare with a control group

pitfalls.symptom: An A/B test declared a winner after two days, then reversed
pitfalls.cause: Peeking and stopping early on noisy data
pitfalls.fix: Fix the sample size and duration in advance, and decide against guardrail metrics

scenarios.title: Financial guidance, new model version
scenarios.situation: An assistant gives account guidance to retail customers, 20,000 requests a day. A new model version passes the offline suite. A wrong answer has regulatory consequences.
unknowns: Can requests be mirrored at a gateway?
scenarios.question: How do you roll the new version out?

options.name: Shadow with sampled scoring, then a 1% canary with stop-loss, then A/B if needed
options.why: Shadow exposes no one, and the canary adds real outcomes behind guardrails.
options.tradeoff: Slower rollout, doubled model cost during shadow and gateway work to mirror.

options.name: A/B test at 50% from day one
options.why: Half the customers could see a worse version of regulated guidance.
options.tradeoff: Right when harm is low and rollback is instant.

options.name: Big-bang release with monitoring
options.tradeoff: All users exposed before any real evidence and slow to detect harm.

flips.then: Start with a very small canary and sampled human review.

flips.if: The change is only a cost-saving model swap with equal offline results
flips.then: A shorter canary may be enough.

scenarios.takeaway: High harm means shadow first, then a tiny canary.

scenarios.title: Copy assistant, millions of requests, low harm
scenarios.situation: A marketing copy assistant handles two million requests a day. Rollback is a flag flip. The team wants to know whether a new prompt raises the share of drafts users accept.
unknowns: What acceptance rate and difference matter?
scenarios.question: Which online method do you use?

options.name: A/B test with sticky assignment, preset sample size and guardrail metrics
options.why: Traffic supports small effects, the outcome metric is direct and rollback is cheap.
options.tradeoff: Some users see the worse prompt for the test duration.

options.name: Shadow only
options.why: It cannot measure acceptance because no user sees the draft.
options.tradeoff: Shadow is right when exposure is unacceptable.

options.name: Judge-scored sampling only
options.why: No exposure and gives a quality trend.
options.tradeoff: Judge preference may not match what users accept.

flips.then: Add a canary stage and safety guardrails first.
An A/B test would take too long, so use a canary and sampled review.

scenarios.takeaway: Big traffic and low harm make A/B the best-evidence method.

scenarios.title: Internal tool, 200 requests a day
scenarios.situation: An internal HR assistant gets about 200 requests a day from 80 employees. The team wants to know if a new retrieval setting helps. Mistakes are embarrassing but not costly.
unknowns: Are users willing to give feedback?
scenarios.question: How do you evaluate the change online?

options.name: Canary by user group for two weeks with sampled review and an offline replay on logged queries
options.why: Traffic is too low for a powered A/B, so combine a controlled exposure with offline replay of real queries.
options.tradeoff: It will detect only large differences.

options.name: A/B test aiming to detect a 3-point difference
options.why: It needs thousands of samples per arm, far beyond 200 requests a day.

options.name: Roll out and read thumbs-down counts

flips.if: The team only needs to avoid harm
flips.then: Run a shadow replay and skip the live exposure.

scenarios.takeaway: Low traffic cannot power small-effect tests.

quiz.q: A new model version must be tested on real inputs, but no customer may see its answers. Which method fits?
quiz.explain: Shadow traffic mirrors requests and discards the new version's responses. A/B and canary expose users, and thumbs need users to see answers.

quiz.q: Using n = 2 x (1.96 + 0.84)^2 x p(1 - p) / d^2 with p = 0.80 and d = 0.10, about how many samples per arm are needed?
quiz.explain: 2 x 7.84 x 0.16 = 2.509, divided by 0.01 gives about 251 per arm. Halving the difference to 0.05 quadruples it to about 1,004.

quiz.q: This shadow plan mirrors production traffic to a new agent version. What is the risk?

code.code:
mirror: 20% of requests -> agent v2 (shadow)
agent v2 tools: send_email, update_ticket, search_kb
responses from v2: discarded

options: v2 will execute its write tools, causing real side effects
quiz.explain: Discarding the response does not stop write tools from running. Use read-only or mocked tools in shadow and compare tool calls instead. The mirror share is not the problem here.

flashcards.back: Shadow mirrors requests to the new version and discards its answers, so users see nothing. Canary sends a small share of users to the new version, so some are exposed.
Maximum mirrored share 50%, one shadow deployment per endpoint, not supported on Kubernetes online endpoints. No Foundry-native shadow feature found on 2026-10-13.

flashcards.front: What are feedback signals good for?
flashcards.back: Triage. Thumbs, edits, retries and escalations are cheap but biased toward vocal users, so use them to find new test cases, not as the only metric.
